title: CDN
body:
A Content Delivery Network is a fleet of geographically distributed servers holding cached copies of static content — images, CSS, JS bundles, video — so a user in Vancouver isn't fetching a logo from a machine in Virginia. The nearest edge node answers instead, cutting latency dramatically.

The conceptually important part for interviews: a CDN node is a **third machine**, belonging neither to you nor to the origin server. It's run by the CDN provider (Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai). This means it can serve stale content after a deploy (hence cache busting and content-hashed filenames), it can generate its own status codes without the origin ever being touched, and it's frequently the TLS termination point too. See [[HTTP Caching]] for the headers that control it.
